setting: A short talk in an earth science class about the water cycle and how climate affects it.
narrator_intro: Listen to part of a talk in an earth science class.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Water on Earth moves in a continuous cycle among oceans, air, and land.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Heat from the sun evaporates water from oceans, lakes, and soil into water vapor.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: As moist air rises and cools, vapor condenses into clouds, and precipitation returns water to the surface.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Some water runs off into rivers; some soaks into the ground and recharges aquifers.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Plants also release vapor through transpiration, which adds moisture to the air.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Climate warming can intensify parts of this cycle: warmer air holds more moisture, so some regions see heavier rain.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: At the same time, other areas may face longer dry spells if storm tracks shift.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Glaciers and snowpack act as seasonal storage; when they shrink, summer river flow can drop.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: So understanding the water cycle helps us predict both floods and droughts under a changing climate.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Next lecture we’ll map how local watersheds connect to this global system.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: How to dig a private swimming pool
options.C: How the water cycle works and how climate can change it

questions.explanation: He explains evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and climate effects.

questions.narrator_text: According to the professor, what starts evaporation?
questions.explanation: He says heat from the sun evaporates water into vapor.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—not the cause he gives.

questions.narrator_text: What does he say warmer air can do?

options.C: Hold more moisture, so some regions see heavier rain

questions.explanation: Warmer air holds more moisture, linked to heavier rain in some regions.

questions.narrator_text: What can be inferred about shrinking glaciers and snowpack?

options.A: They have no link to rivers
options.B: They only affect deserts far from mountains
options.C: They may reduce summer river flow because they store water seasonally
options.D: They increase ocean salt for drinking water

questions.explanation: He says they act as seasonal storage; when they shrink, summer flow can drop.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—he connects them to river flow.
